outcome: Interval between cervical massage and labour onset
cohort: The study included 104 low-risk pregnant women (52 primiparas and 52 multiparas) at a tertiary care hospital in Eastern India who underwent cervical massage once they reached their expected date of delivery.
finding: The majority of women (93%) had a single cervical massage, with pain scores ranging from no pain (31.73%) to moderate pain (16.35%), and only 38.46% would recommend or agree to repeat the procedure despite it showing less discomfort compared to membrane sweeping.
mod_finding: A higher rate of vaginal delivery was noted among multiparas.
